name: Esau
charge: Despising his birthright; marrying Hittite wives; purposing to kill his brother
summary: The firstborn of Isaac sold his birthright for a single meal, took wives of the Canaanites to his parents' grief, and when the blessing went to Jacob resolved to kill him. The prophets and apostles treat him as the pattern of the profane man.
offense: Hebrews names it (Hebrews 12:16-17): a fornicator or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright (Hebrews 12:16). His marriages were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26:35). His hatred of Jacob was murder in the heart (Genesis 27:41).
judgment: He found no place of repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. Malachi: I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste. Obadiah sentences his house for its violence against Jacob: the house of Esau shall be for stubble.

entries.commentary: Abraham took Keturah and had more sons, but Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac; to the sons of the concubines he gave gifts and sent them away eastward from Isaac. The inheritance followed the child of the promise.
Abraham lived an hundred threescore and fifteen years and died in a good old age, as it was prophesied to him; his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah with Sarah.

The generations of Ishmael list twelve princes according to their nations, exactly as the Most High promised in [Genesis 17:20](/bible/genesis/17#v20). Ishmael lived an hundred and thirty and seven years and died in the presence of all his brethren.

Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife. Brothers waiting on a wife, be patient and stay virtuous; Isaac waited forty years, and the Most High had the right sister appointed. Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, and the Lord was intreated of him; Rebekah conceived.

The children struggled together within her, and the Lord gave Rebekah the prophecy: two nations are in thy womb, one people stronger than the other, and the elder shall serve the younger. The whole scripture is good set against evil: the godly against the sinner, Jacob against Esau, righteousness against sin. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb.

The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The scriptures describe the man because a nation comes from him; this teaching identifies Esau's seed with the red, hairy, melanin-lacking people of the world today. Jacob's hand took hold on Esau's heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. When Esau's rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times.

Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. The Most High gives you the characteristics of the man so the nation can be known. Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison, but Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her the prophecy that the younger was the chosen.

Esau sold his birthright for red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, red. He said, What profit shall this birthright do to me, and sware it away for a meal. Thus Esau despised his birthright. Jacob is called a supplanter, but the supplanting was of the Holy Ghost; Esau gave the birthright away himself.

In the famine Isaac was told, Go not down into Egypt; the oath sworn to Abraham was performed unto Isaac: seed as the stars, all these countries, and in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed. In thy seed shall all nations be blessed does not put everybody in the covenant. The seed is Christ, and the children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, scattered into every nation; through Christ scattered Israel in all kindreds of the earth receives repentance and comes back to the Father. The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

Isaac said of Rebekah, She is my sister, fearing the men of the place, and Abimelech saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife and knew. Take the lesson from the sporting: love your wife, play with your wife, keep the flirting and the freshness in the marriage. Give her love, attention, and affection all the days.

Isaac sowed and received in the same year an hundredfold, and the man waxed great until he became very great; and the Philistines envied him and stopped the wells with earth. The nations envy the prosperity of Israel. It is not for anything done to them; the blessing itself is what is hated.
Isaac digged again the wells of his father and the herdmen strove for Esek and Sitnah; he removed and digged Rehoboth, and they strove not: for now the Lord hath made room for us.

Abimelech came saying, We have done unto thee nothing but good, though his people had stopped the wells and sent Isaac away. Isaac answered plainly: Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me? Isaac was not simple; he separated from the people that hated him rather than assimilating among them, and he dealt with their covenant with open eyes. The words can be like butter while war is in the heart.

Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel.

Isaac's eyes were dim so that he could not see, and the Lord allowed that blindness for a purpose: so that the blessing could pass to Jacob. What looks like evil can be for good, as Joseph's slavery in Egypt was for good.

Rebekah heard and moved for Jacob because she carried the word from the Lord: the elder shall serve the younger. She knew the blessing belonged to Jacob by prophecy, and she took the curse upon herself: Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice.
His mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved. Rebekah knew exactly how her husband loved his food and made it to that standard; sisters, learn to prepare it such as he loveth.
Rebekah put Esau's raiment on Jacob and the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands and neck, and Isaac discerned him not: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

The blessing is rulership of the earth: the dew of heaven, the fatness of the earth, plenty of corn and wine; let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee; be lord over thy brethren; cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.

Esau cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry and begged, Bless me, even me also, O my father. But he had already sold the birthright and never dealt rightly with Jacob about it; he wanted the blessing anyway. Esau found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears. He that despised the birthright for one morsel of meat was rejected when he would have inherited the blessing.

Esau's portion: the fatness of the earth and the dew of heaven from above, and by thy sword shalt thou live. Esau's kingdoms have gotten what they have through war; his living is by the sword, by ever more advanced weaponry, and the nations are overcome and awed by it. And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: this is the time period now, where Esau has the dominion and rules first, and when his rule is done, Jacob comes into power.

Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and purposed in his heart to slay him, the same hatred Cain had for Abel. Good against evil runs from the beginning of the book to the end. Rebekah sent Jacob to Laban her brother until Esau's fury turned away, and said she was weary of her life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me? Marrying the sons and daughters within the kindred is a weighty matter to the mothers of Israel. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

The vision of Obadiah, and it is spoken concerning Edom: Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle. Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.

If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, would they not have stolen till they had enough? If the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes? But Esau is searched out, and his hidden things sought up. All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border; the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee. They that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee. Shall I not in that day destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.

For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them. Esau stood on the other side and took part. Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance; neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway to cut off those of his that did escape, nor have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.

For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. As ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually; they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau, and they of the plain the Philistines; and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria; and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. Saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom)

verses.text: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob,
And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.
As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
